title: Second Home vs Investment Property Loan in South Carolina
description: How lenders decide if your beach house is a second home or an investment property, whether you can rent it out, and what the label changes in SC.
h1: Second Home or Investment Property? How Lenders Classify Your Beach House

faq.q: Can I rent out my second home?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae allows a second home loan when the home earns rental income, as long as you live there part of the year, keep control of who stays there, and do not use the rent to qualify for the loan.

faq.q: How many days a year must I live in a second home?
faq.a: Fannie Mae does not set a number of days. It requires that you occupy the home for some portion of the year and that it is suitable for year-round use. We document your plan at application.

faq.q: Can a condo in a rental program be a second home?
faq.a: Not if the program gives a management company control over who stays in the unit, such as a required rental pool with blackout dates for owners. That makes it an investment property, and the building itself may not qualify for a conventional loan.

faq.q: Is the down payment bigger on an investment property?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae allows a smaller down payment on a second home than on an investment property. We give you the exact figure for your loan at pre-approval.

faq.q: Is a second home taxed more in South Carolina?
faq.a: Yes. South Carolina assesses a legal residence at 4% of market value, if the owner applies, and other residential property, including a second home, at 6%.

faq.q: Can I use expected rent to qualify for a second home loan?
faq.a: No. If you need the rent to qualify, the loan is an investment property loan. A DSCR loan, which qualifies you on the property's rent, is one option for an investment purchase.
